newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said Commissioner Hans van den Broek had declared that the Bosnian Serbs would not receive any additional aid from the EU until indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic was arrested.
Spokesman Gerry Kieley briefed on the proposal adopted by the Commission to maintain the compulsory cereals setaside rate for the 1998 harvest at five percent.

Spokesman Willy Helin said the Commission was confident that Boeing would come up with adequate remedies to its proposed merger with McDonnell Douglas. But Helin said that it was up to the company, not the Commission, to decide what those remedies would be.
Spokesman Jochen Kubosch briefed on the Court of Justice judgments.
Spokesman Peter Jorgensen briefed on the Commission reviews of environmental standards in Autria, Finland and Sweden.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/621: Internet: PHARE and TACIS transparency measures prove successful.
- IP/97/622: CLAB Europa: A European database on unfair terms in consumer contracts.
- IP/97/632: New Commission initiative to tackle late payments in commercial transactions.
- IP/97/633: EU reviews environmental standards in the new member states.
- Eurostat news release No 50/97: EU energy consumption up 3.6%.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Energy and industry No 1997-16: Statistical aspects of the energy economy in 1996.
- Eurostat - Statistics in focus - Energy and industry No 1997-17: Extract from "Monthly panorama of European industry 6/97".
